pages.title: Screenshot beautification, on your device
pages.seoTitle: Screenshot editor features, local processing and privacy
pages.description: ScreenHello is a free, local-first screenshot and visual card editor. Add backgrounds, frames, 3D perspective, code and text cards, 18 scene templates, watermarks and local GIF export without uploading.
sections: From a screenshot to a finished visual

Import a local image, paste from the clipboard, try the bundled example, or start from the welcome shortcuts with a code card, text/social card, or one of 18 built-in scene templates. Add padding, backgrounds, 3D perspective, browser frames, text or image logo watermarks and annotations for launches, tutorials and social posts. Everything runs on your device; no account or cloud sync is required.

sections.p: Build syntax-highlighted code cards (14 languages, 6 themes, line highlights and +/- diff mode) or social, quote and changelog cards, or apply any of 18 scene templates in one undoable step. Combine with solid colours, gradients, bundled backdrops or your own local image.

Switch between 8 live-preview 3D perspective presets, browser chrome or optional raster device frames. Add text or locally compressed image logo watermarks (<= 64 KiB), arrows, step numbers and magnifiers.

sections.note: Everything runs in your browser. There is no account, no upload and no cloud sync, so a screenshot never leaves your device.

sections: Edit once. Keep the project.

Arrange up to 12 image or card layers, toggle layer visibility without deleting, undo changes and save a portable .screenhello project (preserving code/text card metadata, 3D perspective and logo watermarks). A project file is your own backup; an automatically saved browser draft is a separate local copy and may be cleared by the browser.
A Web tool with clear boundaries

Export PNG, JPG or WebP with local compression previews, standard AVIF, or render 5 seamless looped micro-animations to local GIF89a (and browser-supported WebM). The Web editor is the available workflow described here. Desktop builds are still test candidates, and a Chrome/Edge extension is planned, not offered as a released download. AVIF offers standard export only, without quality controls or compression preview.

pages.title: Give your screenshots room to breathe
pages.seoTitle: Screenshot beautification: backgrounds, padding and shadows
pages.description: Add backgrounds, padding, rounded corners, shadows, 3D perspective, code and text cards, logo watermarks and annotations locally in ScreenHello. Keep edits reversible and export the complete canvas.
sections: 1. Bring in an image or create a card

Choose a local file, drop it into the welcome area, paste an image, or use the welcome quick-create shortcuts to build a code card (14 languages, 6 themes, line range highlights and +/- diff mode), a text/social card (social post, quote poster or changelog), or open the 18-template scene gallery. Screen capture asks for browser permission. The example button loads a portrait sample on narrow screens and a landscape sample on wider windows.

sections.h: Work with up to 12 layers and visibility toggles
sections.p: A project holds at most 12 image or card layers. Each one keeps its own position, size and appearance settings, and you can hide or show any layer from the layer list without deleting it—hidden layers stay out of interaction and export and participate in undo/redo.
Drive the editor without leaving the keyboard. On macOS use Command wherever the table says Ctrl.

sections.note: Shortcuts are ignored while you are typing in a text field, so they never interrupt a label you are editing.

sections: 2. Build a consistent style and apply templates

Set canvas sizes (including 1.618:1 golden ratio, OG 1200×630, Product Hunt, Xiaohongshu and LinkedIn presets), padding, corner radius, shadow and inner border. Choose a solid colour, gradient, bundled backdrop or local background, or apply any of 18 built-in scene templates atomically in one undoable step. Add text or locally compressed image logo watermarks (<= 64 KiB, 9-grid or tiled), arrows, step numbers and magnifiers, and save reusable styles as local presets.
3. Export static visuals or looped motion

Choose PNG for a transparent canvas, or JPG, WebP and AVIF for the other static workflows (JPEG and WebP flatten transparency to white). For launch teasers or social loops, open File → Export motion to preview 5 seamless micro-animations and encode GIF89a or WebM locally. Zoom changes only the editing view; export scale changes the final pixel dimensions.

pages.title: Browser frames, 3D perspective and device mockups
pages.seoTitle: Browser frames, 3D perspective and device mockups
pages.description: Frame a screenshot with browser chrome, 8 live-preview 3D perspective presets and custom angles in ScreenHello. Learn how device availability, mutual exclusion, fitting and licences work.
sections: Browser chrome and 3D perspective, without fetching URLs

Choose a browser frame from the left panel, enter the address shown in the title bar and adjust the toolbar size; the displayed address is decoration and ScreenHello never visits or captures that website. The left panel also provides 8 live-preview 3D perspective presets plus custom X/Y/Z rotation and perspective distance sliders, rendered locally and preserved in exports and undo history.

sections.h: Browser chrome, 3D perspective and device frames
sections.p: Browser chrome and 3D perspective need no external assets. Selecting a raster device frame automatically resets 3D perspective to flat, while picking a 3D perspective preset switches an active device frame to minimal browser chrome so output stays predictable.

sections.note: Raster device frames come from an optional local pack. When the pack is not installed the picker says so instead of showing an empty list, and every other feature keeps working.

sections: Devices depend on installed artwork

The frame picker shows only artwork available in the current build. Some local installations include MacBook Air M2, iMac 24-inch, Surface Pro, Surface Studio or Pixel 9 Pro variants. These are not guaranteed in the public distribution; available colour choices also depend on the installed pack.
Preserve proportions and respect licences

Use contain to keep the entire screenshot, cover to fill the display with cropping, or stretch when distortion is acceptable. Optional artwork has its own licence; the application's code licence does not automatically cover it. A saved project stores a device identifier, not the optional device pack. Missing artwork must be installed or replaced before a complete export.

pages.title: Image compression and local motion export
pages.seoTitle: PNG, JPG and WebP compression and export guide
pages.description: Compare PNG lossless optimisation and lossy palette reduction, WebP lossless and quality-controlled exports, plus local GIF89a and WebM micro-animation export limits in ScreenHello.
sections: Lossless is not the same as quality 100

PNG lossless optimisation preserves pixels but does not guarantee a smaller file. PNG lossy mode reduces the palette to 256, 128 or 64 colours and may change gradients and translucent shadows. WebP has a true lossless option; JPG and WebP quality sliders are lossy, even at 100. WebP export flattens transparency to white before encoding. AVIF offers standard export only, without quality controls or compression preview.

sections.p: Standard export uses the format’s default encoding settings. PNG and WebP offer lossless modes; JPG and WebP offer adjustable lossy quality. AVIF offers standard export only, without quality controls or compression preview.
These numbers are enforced by the editor before a download starts.

sections.h: Micro-animations and local GIF / WebM export
sections.p: Preview 5 seamless looped micro-animations (Float, Breathing, 3D Sway, Pan and Zoom; 2s, 3s or 4s at 15 or 24 fps). GIF89a is encoded locally inside a Web Worker; WebM is offered only when your browser’s MediaRecorder supports WebM. Motion export renders the current canvas locally and is not a general video upload or transcoding service.

sections.note: AVIF is standard export only: no quality control and no compression preview.

sections: Compare the same composition

Open Export and generate a preview. Compare the standard export and compressed result at the same canvas size, inspect at 100%, and read the actual byte size. The reference is the rendered composition, not the imported original. A larger result is reported honestly. Downloading a valid preview reuses those exact bytes.
Limits and local processing

AVIF offers standard export only, without quality controls or compression preview. Compressed PNG/JPG/WebP downloads allow 4,194,304 pixels. Full previews for PNG/JPG/WebP allow 1,048,576 pixels. When preview is unavailable, direct downloads remain available within their size limit. Standard PNG/JPG/WebP allow 16,777,216 pixels; standard AVIF allows 4,194,304 pixels. Each side is limited to 8192 pixels. Reduce canvas size or scale when necessary. Encoders load from this site on first use and run locally. Batch processing accepts up to 12 images and downloads successful results in a ZIP.

pages.title: Your first ScreenHello project
pages.seoTitle: How to use ScreenHello: import, beautify and export
pages.description: Learn to import images, create code or text cards, apply scene templates and 3D perspective, save portable projects and export static or looped GIF visuals locally.
sections: 1. Open an example, import an image or create a card

Use Open editor on this page, then select Try an example in the centre of the canvas, or click the welcome quick-create shortcuts for a Code card, Text card or Scene templates. To use your own screenshot, choose Choose image and pick a local file. Continue once your content appears in the central canvas.
2. Set background, frame, 3D perspective and watermark

Use Background on the right to choose a solid colour, gradient or image, adjust padding, corners, shadow and text or image logo watermark, and toggle layer visibility in the layer list. Set canvas size, browser frame, 3D perspective presets or browse 18 scene templates on the left. Use bottom tools for annotations when needed.
3. Check dimensions and download an image or loop

Select Export at the top, choose PNG, standard export and 1× scale, check the final pixel dimensions and select Download image. For looped motion, open File → Export motion to preview an animation and encode GIF89a or WebM locally. Canvas zoom does not change output dimensions; 2× scale doubles both width and height.
4. Save an editable project

Choose Save project in the File menu to save a .screenhello file. Downloaded images and GIFs are finished outputs; the project file preserves editable layers, visibility states, code/text card settings, 3D perspective and logo watermarks. Later, use File → Open project to resume editing.
Save a file, not just a draft

Use File → Save project or Save as for a portable backup. File → Open project restores it. Local drafts and recent projects live in this browser, not in a cloud account. Clearing site data can remove them. Save a project file before clearing storage or moving to another device; transfer that file yourself.
Offline and troubleshooting

After the editor reports offline readiness, its cached core can reopen without a connection. Unused backgrounds, optional devices and encoders may still require a first online load. These guide pages require a connection and are not part of the offline editor cache. If capture or clipboard access is denied, use a local file instead. If export exceeds its budget, lower the canvas dimensions or pixel scale.

pages.title: Your pictures stay on your device
pages.seoTitle: Local image processing, project storage and privacy
pages.description: How ScreenHello processes images, code/text cards, 3D renders, logo watermarks and GIF/WebM motion locally, stores drafts in your browser and loads application resources.
sections: What is processed locally?

Imported images, captured screenshots, canvas editing, code and text card rendering, 3D perspective transforms, custom logo watermarks (<= 64 KiB) and social card avatars (<= 32 KiB), plus image compression and GIF89a/WebM motion encoding all run in your device's browser or local Web Workers. This application has no upload backend, cloud account or cloud synchronisation. Local-first does not mean that loading the website makes no network requests.
What is stored or requested?

Projects, drafts and presets can be stored in IndexedDB (including any local avatar or logo image data you add); language and appearance preferences are saved locally. The browser requests the site code, icons, backgrounds and encoding resources as needed. Hosting providers may process ordinary request metadata such as IP addresses and user agents. This source version adds no analytics SDK, advertising pixel or session recording.
How can I remove or move my data?

Manage drafts, presets and recent projects in the local library, or clear this site's data in browser settings. First save any .screenhello project files you want to keep. Clearing browser data does not delete files already downloaded to your device. External source-code links leave this site and are governed by the destination's policies.
